key_insight: The paper turns finite-horizon quantum state-transfer control into a variational optimization problem, using a hardware-efficient parameterized circuit as a surrogate for the terminal evolution.
engineering_relevance: This offers a near-term-friendly control strategy that avoids explicit time-dependent control synthesis and can be deployed on existing quantum hardware with standard gate sets.
method: Build a hardware-efficient ansatz with alternating single-qubit rotations and entangling gates.
Optimize circuit parameters classically to minimize terminal infidelity against a target state.
Use the parameterized circuit as a surrogate for finite-horizon control rather than enforcing Hamiltonian reachability directly.
evidence_signal: Numerical multi-qubit state-transfer benchmarks in the abstract report high-fidelity transfer and examine the trade-off between expressivity, optimization difficulty, and circuit depth.
watch_item: Performance may degrade as system size and circuit depth grow, since the approach depends on ansatz expressivity and can become harder to optimize.
paper_title: A Variational Surrogate Approach to Finite-Horizon Quantum Control via Hardware-Efficient Ansatz
